headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0050 — SMTO couldn't start this group of commands

html:
SMTO-EXE-0050 — SMTO couldn't start this group of commands

GUID: 3f2effe1-a028-43f7-8eb4-ec7866c5eb5b
Slug: sequence-ineligible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO planned to run several commands in a row, but one of them didn't pass its checks, so none of them were started. Nothing on the computer was changed by this group.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's result for this group of commands, or open Technical details in this panel, to see which command was rejected and why. The reason names the command and the check it failed, which tells you which of the next steps applies.
  2. If the reason mentions a password, typing input, administrator rights or a terminal, ask SMTO to run that command by itself instead of as part of a group. Grouped commands must run without anyone typing into them, so these commands have to run separately.
  3. If the reason mentions other jobs or earlier changes that aren't settled, let those finish or resolve them in their task before continuing. SMTO won't start new changes while earlier work on the same things is still unresolved.
  4. If the task is stopping or you selected Stop, start a new request when you are ready. A group can't start while its task is being cancelled.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the commands, either together or one at a time, and their results appear in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. None of the grouped commands ran, so you don't need to undo anything on the computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The shell__sequence preflight rejected one step or a shared prerequisite (shell tool excluded, interactive/privileged/terminal execution, prior-result interpolation, temporal guard, conflicting or unknown-effect jobs, cancellation, or a failed child preflight/availability check) before any step in the sequence was started.

What this means

  • Whole-sequence preflight rejected a child or shared prerequisite, including unsupported execution mode, unavailable tool, policy/budget/cancellation, prior-result interpolation or conflicting work, before starting children in that rejected submission. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Whole-sequence preflight rejected a child or shared prerequisite, including unsupported execution mode, unavailable tool, policy/budget/cancellation, prior-result interpolation or conflicting work, before starting children in that rejected submission.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ineligible_step, nested rejection reason and any preserved prefix receipts from earlier attempts; do not mistake this submission's zero starts for no historical effects.

How to fix it

  • Read error, ineligible_step and error_kind in the sequence result to find the failing step and reason. Fix that cause (run interactive, sudo or terminal commands as separate shell__command calls, drop prior-result interpolation such as step-output, previous_result or source_pointer markers, resolve conflicting or unknown-effect jobs listed in job_ids, or address the child's validation/permission result) and resubmit a sequence of captured, noninteractive, unprivileged commands.
  • Inspect the ineligible step and its precise rejection reason. Use supported captured noninteractive commands within the run policy and remaining tool budget.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every remaining child passes current admission while previously completed or uncertain children retain their original receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
